recipes.name: Eggnog Gingerbread Trifle
ingredients_raw: 1 (5.1 ounce) package instant vanilla pudding mix

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) or 325 degrees F (165 degrees C) according to package directions and baking pan material.

Combine cake mix, water, and egg in a bowl; pour into pan size, shape, and material of your choice. Bake according to package directions and pan size, shape, and material, 24 to 37 minutes. Cool completely, about 1 hour.
Meanwhile, place pudding mix in a large bowl; whisk in eggnog for about 2 minutes. Refrigerate pudding until gingerbread cake is cool and ready to assemble trifle.
Whip cream in a separate large bowl until stiff peaks are just about to form. Beat in sugar and vanilla until peaks form.

Crumble ½ gingerbread cake into a trifle or large glass bowl. Spread ½ eggnog pudding over cake, then spread ½ whipped cream on top of pudding. Repeat layers with remaining ½ each gingerbread cake, eggnog pudding, and whipped cream. Refrigerate 6 hours to overnight. Sprinkle top with cranberries and cookie crumbs before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Eggnog Gingerbread Trifle
raw_recipe.description: This eggnog gingerbread trifle recipe combines two of the holiday's best flavors using gingerbread cake mix, gingersnap cookies, and purchased eggnog.

video.description: Make it an eggnog cream and gingerbread cookie-filled holiday, with this beautifully tempting dessert centerpiece. This easy recipe begins by preparing a gingerbread cake mix. Next mix vanilla pudding mix with eggnog, then whip cream with sugar and vanilla. Finally, assemble by layering crumbled cake, then eggnog pudding, then vanilla whipped cream and repeat until all ingredients are used. Chill for 6 hours and serve garnished with a topping of crushed gingersnap cookies, cranberries and nuts. Then stand back and watch as everyone digs in deep for big, thick scoops of holiday-spiced creamy cakey goodness!

review.reviewBody: I made this for Christmas dinner; it was fantastic! I modified by doubling pudding mixture, and adding nutmeg and cinammon to the whip cream. Also, I couldn't find a gingerbread cake mix so I used a spice cake, and added ground ginger and molasses to it and it tasted just like gingerbread. I also made a praline and crumbled it-anyone that wanted it added some on top of thier trifle. Don't add it before or it won't be crunchy! It was a great addition with a bit of crunch. Definitely will make this one again!

This was yummy! Awesome dessert to serve over the holidays to a large group! I improvised a few things… Used a spice cake mix (reduced water to 1-cup+2-tbsp, added ½-cup molasses, 2-tsp of ginger… In the future I may try substituting orange juice for some of the water) baked in 11x15 pan for 28-min at 325 in convection. I used 2 boxes of vanilla pudding mix (one small box, one large box = 5-cups) made with 3-cups of eggnog and 2-cups of milk. The pudding would be too thick and strong tasting with all eggnog... I may use 6-cups of pudding next time. I whipped 4-cups of whipping cream with 2/3-cup of brown sugar, 1-tsp of cinnamon, 1/8-tsp of nutmeg. I layered this masterpiece into very large trifle bowl into 3 layers (cake, pudding, whip cream). On the top layer I crushed 4 Skor bars and sprinkled them on top right before serving (skipped the cookies and cranberries). It was amazing.

This was deeeelicious! I made only a few minor changes. Instead of a boxed gingerbread or spice cake, I found a recipe for a spicy gingerbread cake from scratch. I added a little more than 2 teaspoons vanilla or bourbon to the whipped cream. Instead, I used about 3 or so of Jim Beam Vanilla bourbon. Instead of regular eggnog, I used Vanilla Spice eggnog by Southern Comfort and added some splashes of the Jim Beam Vanilla bourbon to the eggnog pudding mixture. Finally, I left off the cranberries but crushed ginger snaps on top and placed whole ones around the rim of the bowl.

I used a box spice cake mix and added clove and ginger plus molasses to it. I used a jug of store bought eggnog. I made the whip cream as the recipe stated but can use cool whip. I would double the pudding and whip cream mixtures for a large bowl. I added crushed Heath bar candy to top of whip cream layer for more crunch. I sprinkled nutmeg on top layer of whip cream and placed gingersnap cookies around the bowl. I added maraschino cherries on top as well. Holiday heaven in a bowl! Yum.

It was delicious! I followed the tips from other reviewers by doubling the eggnog/jello. I ran out of eggnog and had to use 1 cup of milk. Also added cinnamon and nutmeg to the whipped cream. Everyone loved it and I definitely don’t think the eggnog overpowered it but I love eggnog. Only thing I would change are the cranberries. I didn’t like the texture of dried cranberries with it.

My family loved this recipe. We will be adding it to our Christmas menu. I did use the recommendations of using a 5 oz and 3 oz vanilla pudding with 3 cups of eggnog and 2 cups of milk. I also added cinnamon and nutmeg to both the pudding and the whipped cream. It was simple to make. It made a beautiful presentation and was delicious!

This is fantastic recipe - pretty, simple and festive. The pudding was too thick so I added some milk to thin it. I did three layers of gingerbread, pudding and whipped cream instead of just two because it looks even more fancy. I only used half the sugar because the eggnog pudding is so sweet. I also omitted the cranberries just because I like a cleaner look.

I made this twice so far. Both times it came out great. I made my own gingerbread for it. Made a vanilla cinnamon whipped cream and added a layer of strawberries. Yum. I won 1st place in our Christmas treat bake off last year with this!

I made this yesterday for Thanksgiving and it got rave reviews! Only changes I made were that I used spice cake instead of gingerbread, and I used 2 cups of eggnog and a cup of sweetened condensed milk for the pudding. This was perfect, because it was just a hint eggnog flavor. If you really like the pudding, you're going to want to double it, however I thought the amount was perfect as is. It's also great because you can make it the night before and it tastes better the next day. Definitely making this again for Christmas. Thanks!

this was excellent! not to rich or sweet, flavors/textures were well balanced. i layered this in a 9x13 pan for co-workers. i used sewing thread to cut the cake in half for layering. found gingerbread cake mix too! it wasnt on the baking isle but was on a center isle display of holiday specialty items, at Walmart!

I thought this was awesome! Don't bother to eat it the first day - it will be just so-so. The next day, after the flavors have had time to meld, it's much better! I used lowfat eggnog, and my pudding was not runny at all (will do that again!). To save time (and fat), I used an 8-oz. tub of Lite Cool Whip (which means, omit the sugar and vanilla) - worked just fine! Gingerbread cookie crumbs on top made it look so pretty. Thanks for the recipe!
I liked it, but it wasn't that popular with others.
Good recipe, however, if you have a larger trifle bowl you need to double everything!!!! I made this for a party and when I finished, my bowl was half full - a bit disappointing!!!!!
Easy and oh so delicious! Makes a beautiful presentation too!
Delicious! Made exactly as listed. Makes a big trifle bowl, but was serving family for T'giving. Will make again. Wish I had eggnog and I'd make it now in April!

To be honest I was leary about trying this recipe. I chose it because I wanted to make some mini trifle cups for a Christmas party and it fit the occasion perfectly. I'm glad I gave it a try. The egg nog was no where near as overpowering or sickeningly sweet as I thought it would be. I actually liked it and the cups turned out cute. I followed the recipe other than having to use a boxed spice cake (the store was out of gingerbread cake mixes) and lightly sprinkling crushed graham cracker ontop as a garnish (I didn't have gingerbread cookies to crush). This one is a keeper.
It was the rave of our holiday potluck dinner. I topped mine with the tiny gingerbread men sprinkles! I'm making it again for New Years Eve!

Delicious and so easy! As Per other reviews, I used light eggnog with the vanilla pudding and it was perfect. Also used spice cake as I couldn’t find gingerbread cake. Topped with ginger snaps and it was excellent!

Made this for a Christmas party and took what was left to work to share the next day, and people raved over it!! I decreased the sugar in the whipped cream to about 2 tablespoons, and it was still plenty sweet with the pudding mix and egg nog. Was hard to find gingerbread cake mix, and the Betty Crocker brand I did find was too mild—-wish I had thought to add extra spices.
It tastes like Christmas ???
